item.title: Direct observation of the Lindhard continuum using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78503-y

In metals, the continuum of electron-hole excitations is described by the Lindhard function. Here, the authors directly observe the corresponding Lindhard continuum in the weakly correlated metal MgB2 using ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering.
item.dc:title: Direct observation of the Lindhard continuum using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering

item.title: Three-photon population imaging of subcortical brain regions
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78585-8

Imaging large cell populations below the cortex in the intact brain is key for understanding brain function. LIFT, a multiscale three-photon microscope, tracks activity in over 1,500 cells across the hippocampus and adjacent regions in behaving mice.
item.dc:title: Three-photon population imaging of subcortical brain regions
